summary: Adelheid Herrmann-Pfandt specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She studied at Bonn, Erlangen-Nuremberg, the Manjushree Centre of Tibetan Culture, and Marburg. She held positions as a Käthe-Leichter-Gastprofessorin at Vienna (~2008–2009) and Privatdozentin at Marburg (2009).

Adelheid Mette worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. She earned her doctorate and Habilitation at Hamburg, studying under Ludwig Alsdorf. She held professorships at Münster (1971; chair and director 1988–2000) and Munich (1978, 1980), later teaching there in 2000.

Aden Kumler is a historian and archaeologist who studied at Chicago, Toronto, Harvard, and the Pontifical Institute of Mediaeval Studies. She served as Assistant Professor at the University of Chicago (2007–2020) before becoming Professor at the University of Basel in 2020.
Adeu Rinpoche was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers Samten Gyatso and Chögon Rinpoche, and he taught Tsoknyi Rinpoche.

Adhémard Leclère worked in religious studies, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He founded The Proletarian, La Typographie française, and the Société Ethnologique de Paris, where he was vice-president, and served as Résident de France at Kratie in Cambodia.

Adinath Neminath Upadhye was an Indologist who studied at the University of Mumbai and Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute. He served at Rajaram College (1930–1962), Shivaji University (1962–1971), and the University of Mysore as founding professor of the Jaina Chair (1971).

Adolf Attenhofer worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Zurich, Geneva, Paris, Berlin, and Munich, where he studied under Ernst Kuhn. He taught at Bündner Kantonsschule (~1906–1932) and founded and directed the Bündner Volkshochschule in 1924.

Adolf Erhart was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Václav Machek at the Masaryk University Faculty of Arts (1945–1949). He later served as a professor at Masaryk University from 1988 to 1993.

Adolf Erman was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Leipzig and Berlin, including under Georg Ebers. He held posts at the Egyptian Museum of Berlin (~1883–1914) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1883–1923).
Adolf Faust was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Strasbourg by 1877. He subsequently worked as a school-teacher (Professor) at Gymnasium Mulhouse.

Adolf Friedrich worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Goethe University Frankfurt under Leo Frobenius and Hermann Lommel, obtaining his Ph.D. in 1939. He served as Privatdozent at Vienna (1942) and Mainz (1946), later working at Frankfurt (~1950–1954).
Adolf Friedrich Hermann Paul Gärtchen was a linguist who earned his PhD from the University of Breslau (1900–1905), where he studied under Otto Hoffmann and Alfred Hillebrandt.

Adolf Friedrich Stenzler was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Greifswald, Bonn, Berlin, and Paris under scholars including Bopp, Schlegel, Kosegarten, Chézy, and Silvestre de Sacy. He served as professor (1833–1847) and Rektor (1862–1863) at Breslau.

Adolf Friedrich von Schack was an Indologist and specialist in Iranian and Central Asian studies. Between 1833 and 1838, he completed law studies at the University of Bonn, Heidelberg University, and Humboldt University of Berlin.

Adolf Holtzmann studied theology and Indology at Halle-Wittenberg, Berlin, Munich, and Paris under Schleiermacher, Frank, Schmeller, and Burnouf. He taught at Bismarck-Gymnasium Karlsruhe (1837) and served as professor of German literature and Sanskrit at Heidelberg University (1852–1870).

Adolf Holtzmann Jr. was an Indologist who studied at Heidelberg under Adolf Holtzmann, Erlangen-Nuremberg under Friedrich von Spiegel, and Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth. He spent his career at the University of Freiburg, becoming Professor of Sanskrit (1908–1914).

Adolf Janáček was an Indologist and linguist. He pursued his education at Charles University, completing his Ph.D. around 1920–1924, and also studied at its Faculty of Arts, First Faculty of Medicine, and Examination Board for Teachers at Secondary Schools.

Adolf Kaegi was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Zurich, Leipzig, and Tübingen under scholars including Schweizer-Sidler and Roth. He taught at Kantonsschule Rämibühl and the University of Zurich, where he became an extraordinary professor and Honorarprofessor (1893–1914).

Adolf Kiessling studied under Friedrich Gottlieb Welcker (~1856–1858). During his career, he held academic posts at the University of Basel (~1869–1877), the University of Greifswald (~1877–1889), and the University of Göttingen.

Adolf Kirchhoff was a linguist, historian, and archaeologist who studied under Karl Lachmann and August Boeckh at Berlin (1842–1846). He taught at Joachimsthalsches Gymnasium (1846) and became ordinary professor at Berlin in 1865, serving until ~1908.
